verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both studies report a correlation between circulating irisin and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) in the same direction of comparison (irisin vs HbA1c), but with opposite signs: study A reports a positive correlation (sentence 10: 'irisin levels positively correlated with ... HbA1c levels'), while study B reports a negative correlation (sentence 9: 'glycated hemoglobin (r = -0.283; p = 0.024)'). Both use correlation analysis without adjustment, and both measure circulating irisin (serum vs plasma) against glycated hemoglobin. The populations differ (FPLD2/OND/HC vs BMI-stratified surgical patients), but this is a population difference, not a text-supported explanation for the opposite sign. No explicit no-effect conclusion is present in either abstract. The findings are genuinely opposite with sufficient comparability and no supported contextual difference.

source_evidence.quote: In the entire study group, irisin levels positively correlated with BMI, lean body mass and index, intra-abdominal/total abdominal fat ratio, triglyceride, cholesterol, insulin, glucose and HbA1c levels.

Irisin was negatively correlated with weight (r = -0.246; p = 0.042), waist circumference (r = -0.272; p = 0.024), glucose (r = -0.259; p = 0.039), glycated hemoglobin (r = -0.283; p = 0.024), triglycerides (r = -0.414; p = 0.024), and positively correlated with HDL (r = 0.280; p = 0.029).

diagnostics.notes: Extraction on both sides correctly reflects the source: A reports positive correlation with HbA1c, B reports negative correlation with glycated hemoglobin. Both are directional assertions from correlation analysis. Populations and sample types differ but comparability of the irisin-HbA1c association contrast is sufficient.
